items.markdown:
The primary byproduct of alcohol (ethanol) metabolism is **acetaldehyde** , which is quickly converted into **acetate** and eventually broken down into **carbon dioxide and water**.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXrLmzY1CcAb4Otihu_d31uwvP-nsaTV81yFbcdMg9Acem-uEyDV6cm4imceXbHXfRGzEZIFVmrSOR-J40GRACuKEMzFHlKezYYqO6pu9iv44G9IwNtLk50LAeTUJ9L3gZvYVglgzSTkIuCNbNAKwmCIM)

According to the [National Institute on Alcohol Abuse and Alcoholism (NIAAA)](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXrLmzY1CcAb4Otihu_d31uwvP-nsaTV81yFbcdMg9Acem-uEyDV6cm4imceXbHXfRGzEZIFVmrSOR-J40GRACuKEMzFHlKezYYqO6pu9iv44G9IwNtLk50LAeTUJ9L3gZvYVglgzSTkIuCNbNAKwmCIM) , the body breaks down ethanol in distinct steps, primarily in the liver:[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXrLmzY1CcAb4Otihu_d31uwvP-nsaTV81yFbcdMg9Acem-uEyDV6cm4imceXbHXfRGzEZIFVmrSOR-J40GRACuKEMzFHlKezYYqO6pu9iv44G9IwNtLk50LAeTUJ9L3gZvYVglgzSTkIuCNbNAKwmCIM)

- **Acetaldehyde:** Formed first when enzymes—mainly alcohol dehydrogenase (ADH), along with CYP2E1 and catalase—oxidize ethanol. It is toxic, reactive, and a known carcinogen that contributes to cell damage and unpleasant effects like flushing or hangover symptoms.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXi31Np1LWpGaR4Mf76eZs-7Y4AdaqsYVCN2h2i5IM3ZzQ8NUYzZw09vVeAIM9OPS5VRQTwygM1lXhI8bLpXs1lOa2enOeiENABcNTyZGKLP7D5c1nmnCmoWuNs1DqRuN-Wzv_uW6KP6Lp)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXrLmzY1CcAb4Otihu_d31uwvP-nsaTV81yFbcdMg9Acem-uEyDV6cm4imceXbHXfRGzEZIFVmrSOR-J40GRACuKEMzFHlKezYYqO6pu9iv44G9IwNtLk50LAeTUJ9L3gZvYVglgzSTkIuCNbNAKwmCIM)[[3]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESjAEBxCJF1xI_WHpaAdsvftg-4rGdzcN8mHvuVSCOPjSC28Jo33-f6MXK3Dt7C5ke33JINIhOeb51GCdz1OsE0YCsRo1zeOh2yCdyJ4-HK9toHyYm_-OGK0L-UMyMAp-wsnYS18wc63Jjl3ofZnCXhdHKYL_wyVWw3qZr8OWG_3L0j1D6wRIK9kWNvL3orQ)[[4]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXtaE4MgWGYQO_N6PYlbdkfxPrYvCG55i7nRPkj5liOh9-YsVpR0EYtpIhW3_J9Dt-aEvC17-Min0X6AY3CnJZLDIEYAM3R9zWNHGDlP0IU9vQXxu2I5S1SNJABQ7MR39yPRj6R1nxGlfA)
- **Acetate:** Formed next when aldehyde dehydrogenase (ALDH) rapidly breaks down acetaldehyde into a less toxic compound . Acetate leaves the liver and is processed into **carbon dioxide and water** in other tissues for elimination.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESdgHEIkXXrLmzY1CcAb4Otihu_d31uwvP-nsaTV81yFbcdMg9Acem-uEyDV6cm4imceXbHXfRGzEZIFVmrSOR-J40GRACuKEMzFHlKezYYqO6pu9iv44G9IwNtLk50LAeTUJ9L3gZvYVglgzSTkIuCNbNAKwmCIM)[[2]](https://study.com/academy/lesson/video/alcohol-metabolism-process-effects.html)

As detailed in scientific reviews on [alcohol metabolism](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXi31Np1LWpGaR4Mf76eZs-7Y4AdaqsYVCN2h2i5IM3ZzQ8NUYzZw09vVeAIM9OPS5VRQTwygM1lXhI8bLpXs1lOa2enOeiENABcNTyZGKLP7D5c1nmnCmoWuNs1DqRuN-Wzv_uW6KP6Lp) and [dangerous byproducts of alcohol breakdown](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXtaE4MgWGYQO_N6PYlbdkfxPrYvCG55i7nRPkj5liOh9-YsVpR0EYtpIhW3_J9Dt-aEvC17-Min0X6AY3CnJZLDIEYAM3R9zWNHGDlP0IU9vQXxu2I5S1SNJABQ7MR39yPRj6R1nxGlfA) , other byproducts and related compounds also form during the process:

- **NADH and reactive oxygen species (ROS):** Converting ethanol and acetaldehyde shifts cellular balance toward NADH and generates oxygen radicals (such as hydroxyethyl radicals), contributing to oxidative stress and fat accumulation.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXtaE4MgWGYQO_N6PYlbdkfxPrYvCG55i7nRPkj5liOh9-YsVpR0EYtpIhW3_J9Dt-aEvC17-Min0X6AY3CnJZLDIEYAM3R9zWNHGDlP0IU9vQXxu2I5S1SNJABQ7MR39yPRj6R1nxGlfA)[[2]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXi31Np1LWpGaR4Mf76eZs-7Y4AdaqsYVCN2h2i5IM3ZzQ8NUYzZw09vVeAIM9OPS5VRQTwygM1lXhI8bLpXs1lOa2enOeiENABcNTyZGKLP7D5c1nmnCmoWuNs1DqRuN-Wzv_uW6KP6Lp)[[3]](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=TCBW-Nidevk&t=40)
- **Adducts:** Reactive aldehydes and oxygen radicals can bind to proteins, lipids, or DNA to form hybrid molecules called adducts, which play a role in tissue injury.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESbgHEIkXXtaE4MgWGYQO_N6PYlbdkfxPrYvCG55i7nRPkj5liOh9-YsVpR0EYtpIhW3_J9Dt-aEvC17-Min0X6AY3CnJZLDIEYAM3R9zWNHGDlP0IU9vQXxu2I5S1SNJABQ7MR39yPRj6R1nxGlfA)
- **Fatty acid ethyl esters (FAEEs):** Smaller amounts of ethanol combine with fatty acids through non-oxidative pathways to form FAEEs.[[1]](https://google.com/goto?url=CAESqAEBxCJF1yKhHd-QtHCaRxOobrmNumw4oQeiqs5luqobxCcM0TSxkYbREG8dUYT_ZKq5F1gYYUwoKLlYLHwVmrVab2YwskD-2x6er-0jSql9-HTXPEGVxjTBiTDhrazwBMrMe2EhNB-R_6I2Rt4Ifs6KWki_TY3KrbKzn7zm9YsWdMfXVYDfIRgi6bGxQiSfhisPcEPhhOfIkYJVSm8IEcBLC4-ehFodOM0)

items.description: More than 90% of the ethyl alcohol that enters the body is completely oxidized to acetic acid. This process occurs primarily in the liver. Read more
